key_insight: Multilingual multimodal machine learning can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech from either language.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support faster, language-flexible screening for bilingual patients when specialized bilingual aphasia assessment is limited.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients were recorded describing a picture in both dominant and non-dominant language.
Four feature sets were extracted: speech timing, word-level, linguistic, and image-text congruence.
Multiple classifiers and an ensemble model were tested to separate nfvPPA from lvPPA.
evidence_signal: In this sample, the best F1 macro scores reached 93% with word-level features in the non-dominant language and 92% with the ensemble in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: Results come from a small single-cohort study, so real-world performance and generalizability need validation across larger and more diverse bilingual populations.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
